lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER III. A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They were indeed a queer-looking party that assembled on the bank—the birds with draggled feathers, the animals with their fur clinging close to them, and all dripping wet, cross, and uncomfortable.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first question of course was, how to get dry again: they had a consultation about this, and after a few minutes it seemed quite natural to Alice to find herself talking familiarly with them, as if she had known them all her life. Indeed, she had quite a long argument with the Lory, who at last turned sulky, and would only say,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “I am older than you, and must know better;”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: and this Alice would not allow without knowing how old it was, and, as the Lory positively refused to tell its age, there was no more to be said.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At last the Mouse, who seemed to be a person of authority among them, called out,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Sit down, all of you, and listen to me! I’ll soon make you dry enough!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They all sat down at once, in a large ring, with the Mouse in the middle. Alice kept her eyes anxiously fixed on it, for she felt sure she would catch a bad cold if she did not get dry very soon.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Ahem!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Mouse with an important air,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “are you all ready? This is the driest thing I know. Silence all round, if you please! ‘William the Conqueror, whose cause was favoured by the pope, was soon submitted to by the English, who wanted leaders, and had been of late much accustomed to usurpation and conquest. Edwin and Morcar, the earls of Mercia and Northumbria—’”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Ugh!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Lory, with a shiver.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “I beg your pardon!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Mouse, frowning, but very politely:

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Did you speak?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Not I!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Lory hastily.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “I thought you did,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Mouse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “—I proceed. ‘Edwin and Morcar, the earls of Mercia and Northumbria, declared for him: and even Stigand, the patriotic archbishop of Canterbury, found it advisable—’”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Found what?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Duck.

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “Found it,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Mouse replied rather crossly:

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “of course you know what ‘it’ means.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I know what ‘it’ means well enough, when I find a thing,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Duck:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “it’s generally a frog or a worm. The question is, what did the archbishop find?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Mouse did not notice this question, but hurriedly went on,

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “‘—found it advisable to go with Edgar Atheling to meet William and offer him the crown. William’s conduct at first was moderate. But the insolence of his Normans—’ How are you getting on now, my dear?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: it continued, turning to Alice as it spoke.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “As wet as ever,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice in a melancholy tone:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “it doesn’t seem to dry me at all.”

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “In that case,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Dodo solemnly, rising to its feet,

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “I move that the meeting adjourn, for the immediate adoption of more energetic remedies—”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Speak English!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Eaglet.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I don’t know the meaning of half those long words, and, what’s more, I don’t believe you do either!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And the Eaglet bent down its head to hide a smile: some of the other birds tittered audibly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “What I was going to say,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Dodo in an offended tone,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “was, that the best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “What is a Caucus-race?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice; not that she wanted much to know, but the Dodo had paused as if it thought that somebody ought to speak, and no one else seemed inclined to say anything.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Why,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Dodo,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “the best way to explain it is to do it.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: (And, as you might like to try the thing yourself, some winter day, I will tell you how the Dodo managed it.)

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: First it marked out a race-course, in a sort of circle, (

lines.speaker: Dodo
lines.text: “the exact shape doesn’t matter,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: it said,) and then all the party were placed along the course, here and there. There was no “One, two, three, and away,” but they began running when they liked, and left off when they liked, so that it was not easy to know when the race was over. However, when they had been running half an hour or so, and were quite dry again, the Dodo suddenly called out

lines.speaker: Dodo
lines.text: “The race is over!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: and they all crowded round it, panting, and asking,

lines.speaker: Dodo
lines.text: “But who has won?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This question the Dodo could not answer without a great deal of thought, and it sat for a long time with one finger pressed upon its forehead (the position in which you usually see Shakespeare, in the pictures of him), while the rest waited in silence. At last the Dodo said,

lines.speaker: Dodo
lines.text: “Everybody has won, and all must have prizes.”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “But who is to give the prizes?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: quite a chorus of voices asked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Why, she, of course,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Dodo, pointing to Alice with one finger; and the whole party at once crowded round her, calling out in a confused way,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Prizes! Prizes!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice had no idea what to do, and in despair she put her hand in her pocket, and pulled out a box of comfits, (luckily the salt water had not got into it), and handed them round as prizes. There was exactly one a-piece, all round.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “But she must have a prize herself, you know,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Mouse.

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “Of course,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Dodo replied very gravely.

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “What else have you got in your pocket?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he went on, turning to Alice.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Only a thimble,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice sadly.

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “Hand it over here,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Dodo.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then they all crowded round her once more, while the Dodo solemnly presented the thimble, saying “We beg your acceptance of this elegant thimble;” and, when it had finished this short speech, they all cheered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice thought the whole thing very absurd, but they all looked so grave that she did not dare to laugh; and, as she could not think of anything to say, she simply bowed, and took the thimble, looking as solemn as she could.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The next thing was to eat the comfits: this caused some noise and confusion, as the large birds complained that they could not taste theirs, and the small ones choked and had to be patted on the back. However, it was over at last, and they sat down again in a ring, and begged the Mouse to tell them something more.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “You promised to tell me your history, you know,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “and why it is you hate—C and D,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she added in a whisper, half afraid that it would be offended again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Mine is a long and a sad tale!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Mouse, turning to Alice, and sighing.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “It is a long tail, certainly,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, looking down with wonder at the Mouse’s tail;

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “but why do you call it sad?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And she kept on puzzling about it while the Mouse was speaking, so that her idea of the tale was something like this:—

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text:
“Fury said to a
mouse, That he
met in the
house,
‘Let us
both go to
law: I will
prosecute
you.—Come,
I’ll take no
denial; We
must have a
trial: For
really this
morning I’ve
nothing
to do.’
Said the
mouse to the
cur, ‘Such
a trial,
dear sir,
With
no jury
or judge,
would be
wasting
our
breath.’
‘I’ll be
judge, I’ll
be jury,’
Said
cunning
old Fury:
‘I’ll
try the
whole
cause,
and
condemn
you
to
death.’”

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “You are not attending!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Mouse to Alice severely.

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “What are you thinking of?”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I beg your pardon,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice very humbly:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “you had got to the fifth bend, I think?”

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “I had not!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: cried the Mouse, sharply and very angrily.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “A knot!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice, always ready to make herself useful, and looking anxiously about her.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Oh, do let me help to undo it!”

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “I shall do nothing of the sort,”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Mouse, getting up and walking away.

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “You insult me by talking such nonsense!”

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “I didn’t mean it!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: pleaded poor Alice.

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “But you’re so easily offended, you know!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Mouse only growled in reply.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Please come back and finish your story!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice called after it; and the others all joined in chorus,

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Yes, please do!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: but the Mouse only shook its head impatiently, and walked a little quicker.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “What a pity it wouldn’t stay!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: sighed the Lory, as soon as it was quite out of sight; and an old Crab took the opportunity of saying to her daughter

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Ah, my dear! Let this be a lesson to you never to lose your temper!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “Hold your tongue, Ma!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the young Crab, a little snappishly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: “You’re enough to try the patience of an oyster!”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I wish I had our Dinah here, I know I do!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said Alice aloud, addressing nobody in particular.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “She’d soon fetch it back!”

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “And who is Dinah, if I might venture to ask the question?”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: said the Lory.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Alice replied eagerly, for she was always ready to talk about her pet:

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Dinah’s our cat. And she’s such a capital one for catching mice you can’t think! And oh, I wish you could see her after the birds! Why, she’ll eat a little bird as soon as look at it!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This speech caused a remarkable sensation among the party. Some of the birds hurried off at once: one old Magpie began wrapping itself up very carefully, remarking,

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “I really must be getting home; the night-air doesn’t suit my throat!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: and a Canary called out in a trembling voice to its children,

lines.speaker: Mouse
lines.text: “Come away, my dears! It’s high time you were all in bed!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: On various pretexts they all moved off, and Alice was soon left alone.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “I wish I hadn’t mentioned Dinah!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said to herself in a melancholy tone.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: “Nobody seems to like her, down here, and I’m sure she’s the best cat in the world! Oh, my dear Dinah! I wonder if I shall ever see you any more!”

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And here poor Alice began to cry again, for she felt very lonely and low-spirited. In a little while, however, she again heard a little pattering of footsteps in the distance, and she looked up eagerly, half hoping that the Mouse had changed his mind, and was coming back to finish his story.
